newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares slip late as sellers emerge.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares slip late as sellers emerge.

text.p: Italian shares eased back to end lower on Monday as sellers emerged in late afternoon to give the market a negative stance after stocks on the Milan bourse spent much of the trading day in positive territory, dealers said.

Olivetti was one of the days big losers off 6.34 percent at 613 lire on talk of a possible quotation for mobile phone consortium Omnitel where Olivetti is the biggest shareholder, while San Paolo di Torino suffered from a Goldman Sachs downgrade to slide 6.15 percent to 14,000 lire.
The all-share Mibtel index ended off 0.8 percent at 14,973 and the blue chip Mib30 1.1 percent down at 22,756.
Attention was again on the financial sector and along with San Paolo, Credito Italiano slipped 1.78 percent to 3,538 lire despite a Goldman earnings forecast upgrade.
Ambroveneto ended up 7.99 percent at 9.839 lire ahead of this week's likely details of its rights issue while insurer Generali added 0.71 percent to 38,594 lire.

Also in the banking world, French state-controlled bank Credit Lyonnais CRLIi.PA has finally agreed to sell its 56.8 percent stake in Credito Bergamasco to Banca Popolare di Verona for 1.24 trillion lire.

Retail group Standa ended up 4.55 percent at 19,864 lire after it announced late Friday that its controlling shareholder, Silvio Berlusconi's Fininvest group, was launching a public buy offer (OPA) for all ordinary and savings shares in the company held by minority shareholders.
Edison steadied a little, up 0.17 percent at 8,271 lire, after weakness last week when ENEL said it was to halt buying excess electricity off the private sector.
